transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

The 'U' code on Beko induction hobs typically means the hob cannot detect a suitable pan. This is very often due to the cookware itself rather than a fault with the new appliance. Induction hobs only heat pans made of ferrous metal (like cast iron or magnetic stainless steel) that have a flat base large enough to cover the heating zone. If the pan is aluminium, copper, non-magnetic stainless steel, warped, or too small, it will not be detected and will flash 'U'. Please try these two quick checks:
1. Place a magnet on the bottom of your saucepan. It should stick firmly. If it doesn't slide off easily, the pan is induction-compatible.
2. Check if the hob has a child lock or key pad activated (often shown by a key or padlock symbol). If so, hold that button for 3-5 seconds to unlock it. If you have another pan that you know works on other zones of this hob (or any induction hob), try placing it on this specific zone. Does the 'U' appear with that pan too? This will tell us if the issue is the saucepan or the hob zone itself.

The magnet doesn't stick to my saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole, and the casserole heated fine on that zone. I don't think the child lock is on as the other buttons work. So is it the pans?

Yes, it is the pans. The 'U' code suggests that the hob cannot detect a suitable pan on that zone. Your test with the cast-iron casserole proves the hob itself is working perfectly: because the magnet sticks to the casserole and it heated up fine, we know the induction coil and electronics are functioning correctly. The fact that the magnet does not stick to your saucepan means it is made of a material (likely aluminium or non-magnetic stainless steel) that induction hobs cannot heat. This is not a fault with your new Beko; it simply means those specific saucepans are not compatible with induction cooking. To use this hob, you will need to switch to cookware that has a magnetic base. You can check any pan by holding a magnet against its bottom: if the magnet sticks firmly, the pan will work on your new hob.
